To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a mutation in the Tsc2 gene is the rate‐ limiting step in renal carcinogenesis in Eker rats.
we have established metastatic Eker rat RC cell lines from non‐metastasizing parental cell lines by co‐implanation with a foreign‐body.

we have established two Eker renal carcinoma cell lines, S‐Lk 9d‐SLm and Lk9dL, which have the same genetic background but different metastatic potentials, and that the S‐Lk‐9d‐SL m cell line may be a useful tool to investigate metastasis promoting events in renal carcinomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of tumor metastasis, with the goal of developing effective therapies for the treatment of metastatic disease.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the development and metastasis of RCs.
the genetic basis of renal cancer metastasis in the Eker model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Eker rat is a model that has been used for the study of RCC and that the Eker mutation is the first step in the development of RCC, but that additional genetic events are necessary for metastasis.

the Eker rat provides a model for the investigation of renal carcinogenesis, and the cell lines described here should be valuable tools to study the molecular basis of renal cell carcinoma metastasis.
the Tsc2 mutation in the Eker model of renal carcinogenesis is not sufficient to promote metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Eker rat is an ideal model to study metastasis of RCs.
the Tsc2 mutation is necessary but not sufficient for renal cancer metastasis in the Eker model.
the Eker model is an excellent model for renal carcinogenesis, but not for metastasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Eker rat is a useful model to investigate the metastatic process of renal cancer.
the metastatic variants of Eker RC cell lines can be useful experimental tools for investigating renal cancer metastasis.
we have generated two cell lines from the same parental cell line that differ only in the ability to metastasize.
